river: Chela (Umiam) above the border at Dalia–Kalatek (India)

river: Teesta entry at Khoga Kharibari, Dimla

river: Dolura river sand fan above the border (Balat, India)
note: Rerun with the corrected window. The fan stays bright sand (150–200 ha) with low-flow water near 30 ha; water falls slightly after 2011 (36 to 23 ha, p = 0.002). The 2015–2017 conversion at Dolura (E060) is confined to the reach inside Bangladesh.
Braided border river; channels migrate across the window and water and sand show no significant break (all p > 0.1).

river: Someshwari below Durgapur (Shibganj to Bhanga bridge)

river: Nakugaon land port and the Bhogai entry (Nalitabari, Sherpur)

river: Lafarge Umiam limestone mine at Nongtrai (Meghalaya, India)

river: Lafarge Surma cement plant and limestone yard (Chhatak)

river: Sunamganj Medical College on filled haor land

Braided Teesta. Bars bright to 2019, then vegetate: sand 340 to 65–110 ha by 2024–2025 while vegetation rises from about 150 to 430 ha (break 2019, p = 0.04). As at the other Teesta sites, no extraction signal at 30 m.

river: Kalairag stone pits and yards on the Dhalai east bank (Bholaganj)

Added from imagery. Braided sand bed; sand falls from about 805 to 410 ha after 2011 (p < 0.001) while vegetation rises (about 150 to 450–800 ha); water swings with stage (105 to 366 ha) without a persistent rise. No pit pattern.

Added from imagery as the upstream control for Bholaganj (N04, N23, N47). The bright gorge bed is small and flat for 38 years (bare 5–14 ha in pit-field mode; the river outline holds only 22 ha). Added as a dredging test. Deep single channel; January water flat at about 100 ha for 38 years and almost no sand. Dredging in a channel that is already water at low flow does not change the January areas.

Added from imagery; pit-field mode. Small sand fan at the border with fields and tea; bare ground falls slowly from about 50 to 30 ha after 2011 as the fan vegetates and water stays below 15 ha. No pit field or yard.

Added from imagery (India), the last reach above the border at Dimla. Bright worked patches on the bars in Google imagery are below 30 m. Added from imagery. Barrage pond and the braided bed below it. Sand falls from about 774 to 466 ha after 2009 (p < 0.001) as vegetation rises from about 80 to 480 ha; water swings with stage (100 to 310 ha). Same timing as the Teesta reaches upstream in India (N50 to N52), so the change is river-wide, not local.

Added as a dredging test (dredging of the Surma at Sylhet from 2021). Dredging in a channel already full at low flow does not change the January areas.

Added from imagery, where the Teesta leaves the hills (India); the upstream-most Teesta reach. Sand falls from about 360 to 110–160 ha after 2015 (p = 0.003) as vegetation rises to about 350 ha by 2023; the October 2023 Teesta flood (South Lhonak lake outburst) then re-covers the bars with fresh sand (sand 228–282 ha, vegetation 208–237 ha in 2024–2025). Added from imagery (India). Narrow dry boulder bed with no January water; the outline holds about 106 ha. Bare bed falls from about 55 to 32 ha after 2011 (p < 0.001) as vegetation rises; low confidence. Boulder lifting from a dry bed does not change the January areas.

river: Diana river at the NH17 bridge (Dooars, India)
note: Added from imagery (India). Wide dry boulder bed with no January water in any season. Bare bed and vegetation swing from season to season (sand 32–456 ha) with no persistent change; boulder lifting from a dry bed is not recorded by the January series.

Added from imagery (India); the Torsa becomes the Dudhkumar in Bangladesh. river: Stone crushers and river-bed quarry at Ethelbari–Dangapara (Dooars, India)

river: Lumshnong limestone quarries and cement plants (Meghalaya, India)

river: Jarapata quarry pits by the Sutarkandi land port (Assam, India)

Added as a braided S2 control. Water and sand shift with channel migration; sand falls from about 910 to 640 ha after 2019 (p = 0.05) as bars vegetate (vegetation about 100 to 230–380 ha). Seasons 2006 to 2012 lack a clear January scene; low confidence.

Added from imagery (sand landing ghats). The outline captures only 13 ha of haor-edge channel that floods in some Januaries; the river here is too narrow and too deep for the low-flow method, and the ghats are not resolved.

Added from imagery (India), the wide sandy bed inside Siliguri. Almost no January water. Bare bed falls from about 82 to 53 ha after 2011 (p < 0.001) as vegetation spreads (about 30 to 55–68 ha), with no pit pattern. Bed mining reported in Siliguri does not show as pits at 30 m.

Added from Google Maps and the 2024–2025 press reports of stone looting at Shah Arfin Tila; pit-field mode. The E069 window covers the same ground but was run on the narrow streams. Bare ground rises on the tila from 2001 to 2005 (24 to 91 ha, p < 0.001) and pit lakes appear in 2014: water 7 to 81 ha after 2013 (p < 0.001), reaching 175–185 ha in 2022 and 2024. Stone is dug from the tila and its fan below the water table.

Added from Google Maps; pit-field mode. Unbroken forest to 2004; quarry ground opens in 2005 to 2006 and grows steadily: bare ground 0 to 31 ha after 2005 (p < 0.001), 47–72 ha by 2023–2025. Opens in the same years as the Lumshnong quarries (N65) and the Lafarge mine (N39).

river: Mawmluh limestone quarry at Sohra (Meghalaya, India)
note: Added from Google Maps; pit-field mode. The Mawmluh quarry predates the record (the Cherra cement plant opened in the 1960s), so there is no onset to date. The plateau series swings with grass burning and terrain shadow (mapped water 0–160 ha) and settles after 2011; no persistent rise of quarry ground.

river: Stone quarries and crushers at Dilnapara–Tangoan (West Garo Hills, India)
note: Added from a cluster of stone crusher listings; pit-field mode. Forested hills; bare ground stays below 10 ha after 2011. The brown valley fills seen on recent Google imagery are not classed as bare at NDVI < 0.25, and the crusher yards are small.

river: Diana river sand and stone collection at Dhumpara (Dooars, India)
note: Added from Google Maps (sand and stone collection points). Dry boulder and sand bed with no January water. Bare bed widens after 1998 (227 to 279 ha, p = 0.045) as bed vegetation is stripped, then swings from season to season; the 1998 and 2000 floods can explain the step, and lifting from a dry bed is not recorded.

river: Balason at Lalsara sand processing plant (Siliguri, India)
note: Added from Google Maps (sand processing plant). Dry sand bed; bare bed falls from 339 to 265 ha after 2004 (p < 0.001) as vegetation spreads. Landsat shows small ponds of 2–10 ha after 2012 (p < 0.001), but January–March Sentinel-2 composites (10 m, 2016–2026) show no ponds: the patches are wet low-flow threads. Sentinel-2 does show a fan of haul tracks running onto the bed from the east bank from 2020, with bright worked patches through 2026, consistent with bed lifting below the 30 m method. PlanetScope not checked (needs a Planet login).

Added from imagery; a Dooars river with reported boulder lifting. Dry boulder bed with no January water. Bare bed falls from 284 to 235 ha after 2013 as vegetation rises, but the step coincides with the Landsat 7 to 8 change: same-season ETM+/OLI pairs read NDVI about 0.07 higher on OLI, and with TM/ETM+ harmonised to OLI (Roy et al. 2016) the decline is not significant (250 to 232 ha, p = 0.06). Reclassified from bar vegetation to no signal on 25 Oct 2026. Lifting from a dry bed is not recorded.
Added from imagery. Dry boulder bed with no January water. Bare bed falls from 489 to 323 ha after 2010 (p < 0.001) as vegetation spreads (about 85 to 200–320 ha); no pit pattern.

Added from imagery; boulders from this reach are crushed and exported through Jaigaon. Bare bed falls from 541 to 295 ha after 2013 (p < 0.001) as vegetation rises (about 75 to 270 ha), while the low-flow channel stays at 20–35 ha. The step falls at the 2013–2014 Landsat 7 to 8 change. Same-season ETM+/OLI pairs read NDVI about 0.05 higher on OLI, but with TM/ETM+ harmonised to OLI (Roy et al. 2016) the decline remains (374 to 250 ha after 2013, p < 0.001), so the step is not a sensor effect alone.

river: Sankosh at Lamichey–Majathang stone crusher (Bhutan border)
note: Added from Google Maps (SCL stone crusher plant). A vegetated island in the bed is stripped to bare gravel in 2000–2001 (bare 21 to 110 ha, vegetation 165 to 75 ha, p < 0.001) and the low-flow channel widens (8 to 22 ha); the abrupt single-season change fits the 2000 monsoon flood better than quarrying. No pit pattern; the plant and its stockpiles are below 30 m.

Added from Google Maps (Kushalpur balu mahal, a leased sand quarry). Low-flow water rises from 26 to 42 ha after 2003 while sand falls from 92 to 60 ha (both p < 0.001), and 26 ha of the earlier sand bed is water after 2003 (from 9 ha), without a gain in vegetation until 2012. A step change at a leased sand mahal; channel widening cannot be excluded at 30 m.

Added from Google Maps (Tarapasha balu mahal). The Manu here is about 60 m wide; the outline holds 94 ha, mostly banks and fields, and low-flow water (10–30 ha) swings without a persistent change. Sand lifting in a channel this narrow is below the method.

Added from Google Maps (sand landing ghat). Deep single channel and floodplain whose January water swings with stage (1–105 ha); almost no sand at low flow. The ghat stores sand brought by boat and leaves no trace at 30 m.

river: Sankosh at Jaraguri stone crushers (Assam–West Bengal)
note: Added from a cluster of stone crusher listings (Swastika, Barman, Narzary). Braided boulder bed whose bare and vegetated areas swing from season to season (bare 140–440 ha) without a persistent change; low-flow water stays at 30–90 ha. Lifting from the dry bed is not recorded.

river: Torsa at Hasimara, main channel (Dooars, India)
note: Rerun on 25 Oct 2026 with the window moved 7 km west onto the main braided Torsa channel (the first window fell on a side stream). Bare bed widens from about 215 to 290 ha after 1999 (p = 0.009), after the 1998 floods; low-flow water stays at 10–35 ha (no break, p = 0.62). Bars vegetate briefly in 2014–2016 (sand about 195 ha) and are bare again from 2017. No persistent extraction signal; boulder lifting from the dry bed is not recorded.

river: Burimari land port stone yards (Patgram, Lalmonirhat)
note: Added from news reports and imagery (pit-field mode). Bright stone yards spread along the road south-east of the Burimari land port from 2001–2005 and widen through 2010–2024. The bare series is dominated by fallow paddy; the dating is visual. About 400 crushers were reported running at the port in 2018 (Daily Star, 22 Mar 2018). Google Earth imagery of June 2011 shows yards only beside the port; by 2025 they extend about 2 km south-east along the road. Imported stone, not local extraction.

Added from imagery and news reports of stone lifting around Bhajanpur (TBS, 22 Nov 2022) (pit-field mode). Scattered bright pits appear in the fields from 2001–2005; small ponds rise from about 5 to 13 ha after 2002 (p < 0.001). Bare land falls from 340 to 92 ha after 2013 as tea gardens and crops cover the fallows. Low confidence: most pits are below 30 m.

Added from imagery and reports of dolomite blasting in the Pugli hills (pit-field mode). The grey quarry faces and waste fan are already present in 1989 and change little at 30 m; the bare-ground fall after 2011 and the water swings are hill shadow and the Landsat 7 to 8 change. As at Mawmluh (N71), the quarry predates the record, so no onset is dated.

river: Sand yard on the Borogang floodplain below Jaintiapur
note: Added from Sentinel-2 screening (pit-field mode): a bright sand patch of 10–35 ha beside the channel in 2023. Landsat shows a similar patch on and off from 1989 (6–36 ha) with no lasting change; it is gone in 2025. No persistent extraction signal.

river: Osmani airport expansion fill and stone crusher yards (Sylhet)
note: Added from imagery and reports of the airport expansion (contract May 2020, works from October 2020; TBS, 11 Nov 2023) (pit-field mode). Bright fill appears at the apron by 2014 and along a parallel strip beside the runway by 2017–2018; Sentinel-2 shows the strip bare in 2020 and the new terminal apron filled in 2023. The bare series is dominated by fallow and hill-tea surfaces, so the dating is visual. Stone crusher yards west of the airfield (Al Amana, Shah Vorosha) are below 30 m.

river: Kushiyara at Balaganj with sand dump field
note: Added for reported dredging between Kushiyara Bazar and Paharpur, Balaganj (15–20 dredgers; Daily Star). The pale patch north of the river picked in Sentinel-2 screening is a seasonal beel present since 1989, not a sand dump. Low-flow water follows stage (p = 0.73); no extraction signal at 30 m.

Added from Sentinel-2 screening and reports of the Dhaka–Sylhet highway industrial belt between Shaistaganj and Madhabpur (over 100 factories; TBS, 11 Feb 2023) (pit-field mode). Bright fill pads and factory roofs appear on former paddy land from 2014 and spread through 2018–2024; Sentinel-2 shows new pads in 2026. The bare series is dominated by paddy and flood stage, so the dating is visual; low confidence on the year.

river: Khowai at Rajar Bazar balu mahal (Chunarughat, Habiganj)
note: Added for the Rajarbazar sand quarry, the district's highest-value lease (Tk 15.42 crore in 1432 BS; Daily Star, 24 Jun 2025). Narrow channel (outline 78 ha). Low-flow water rises from 10.5 to 14.8 ha after 2002 (p < 0.001), bare bars fall from 28 to 12 ha after 2010 (p < 0.001), and bars turn to water progressively downstream from about 2000 to 2010 (s2w 2.8 to 5.6 ha, p < 0.001). Consistent with bed lowering by extraction; low confidence at a channel about 60 m wide.

river: Kushiyara at the Sherpur bridge sand landing (Sylhet–Moulvibazar)
note: Added for dredging and the Brahmangram sand stockpile at Sherpur (Daily Star). Deep single channel; low-flow water stays at 60–80 ha (p = 0.23) and bars are small (8–33 ha). The Srihatta Economic Zone fill (N25) shows south-west of the window from 2018. No extraction signal at 30 m.

river: Ganeshwari at Lengura stone dredging (Kalmakanda, Netrokona)
note: Added for reported stone dredging on the Ganeshwari, Mahadeo and Bagla at Lengura (up to 16 dredgers per site; Daily Star, 22 Apr 2013). The channel is about 30–50 m wide; the outline picks up dark forested hill slopes in the north-west as 'water', which drive the water and sand-to-water series. No reliable signal at 30 m.
